entities.name: John Raoul Petraliphas
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John Komnenos Raoul Doukas Angelos Petraliphas was a Byzantine noble and military commander during the reign of Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos, playing a pivotal role in the Fourth Crusade and the capture of Constantinople in 1204.

As the Latin forces besieged the city, Petraliphas led the charge against the Byzantine defenses, ensuring the city's fall to the Crusaders.

The consequences of this event were far-reaching, with the Latin Empire established and the Byzantine Empire's territorial holdings significantly reduced.

The legacy of Petraliphas can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Latin Empire, which would go on to shape the medieval political landscape of the region.

'As the gates of Constantinople swung open to the West, the very fabric of Byzantine power was torn asunder,' Petraliphas's own words would later be quoted by historians as a poignant reminder of the event's enduring impact.
